# Bond Problems and Software Support

Report 200 | Published 2026-10-25 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2026-10-25/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/200.json)

Bond entry yields, monetary dilution and software adaptation.

The local Treasury call and the software-bottom observation are supported. The main analytical weakness is treating a declining share of M2 as a loss of purchasing power. France’s institutional constraints are real, while the proposed crisis pathways and long-term software and gold outcomes remain unresolved.

**Coverage:** Full numbered text and image inventory read. All material theses across macro, digital assets, investment analysis and concluding sections considered. Position listings and incidental descriptive statistics are excluded unless they support a thesis.

### 200-C04

**Yield minus M2 growth measures money-share dilution.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | bond-m2-dilution-arithmetic |
| Source blocks | 27, 30, 31, 33, 35 |
| Thesis family | bond-m2-dilution-arithmetic |

Under a constant nominal return and an M2 denominator growing at a fixed rate, the relative monetary share changes by (1+r)/(1+g)-1. At 5% and 5.7%, that is -0.662%, close to the stated subtraction approximation. A bond’s interim market value and reinvestment returns can differ from its quoted yield.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Deductive assessment:**

- Wealth comillion pounds at 5%
- M2 grows 5.7%
- Compare wealth with aggregate M2, not consumer prices

1.05/1.057 - 1 = -0.0066225; subtraction approximates this as -0.7%.

**Outcome evidence:**

No independent outcome source is recorded. Any deductive assessment is identified separately.

### 200-C05

**Money-share dilution determines purchasing-power performance.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Wrong |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | m2-growth-versus-real-return |
| Source blocks | 33, 37, 38, 40, 41, 42 |
| Thesis family | m2-growth-versus-real-return |

A share of M2 and purchasing power are different quantities. With 5% nominal return, 5.7% M2 growth and 3% price inflation, monetary share falls while purchasing power rises 1.94%. Changes in real output, money demand and velocity prevent the M2 subtraction from being a general real-return measure. This distinction matters to the report’s age-based portfolio conclusions.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [M2SL observations through the audit cutoff](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/M2SL) | FRED / originating statistical agency | Verified in the audit

Monetary aggregate, not a consumption-price index.

- [CPIAUCSL observations through the audit cutoff](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCSL) | FRED / originating statistical agency | Verified in the audit

Consumer price index supplies a separate price denominator.

### 200-C08

**Productivity growth explains gold’s long-run purchasing power.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | gold-productivity-purchasing-power |
| Source blocks | 40 |
| Thesis family | gold-productivity-purchasing-power |

U.S. nonfarm business productivity averaged roughly 2.1% since 1947, but this is not a universal annual human-productivity law. Subtracting gold-stock growth from productivity growth does not determine gold’s real price: investment demand, monetary regimes and substitution also change. The suggested causal model is incomplete.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Productivity and costs](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/pdf/prod2.pdf) | BLS | Verified in the audit

Long-run U.S. nonfarm business productivity growth around 2.1%; substantial cycle and sector variation.

## Analytical tools and charts

- **Crude and crack spreads:** Separate feedstock from refining margin Visual inspection: not performed.
- **Bond dilution rate:** Nominal yield minus M2 growth; not real return Visual inspection: not performed.
- **French-German yield spread:** Country-specific credit and political risk Visual inspection: not performed.
- **FAST Graphs:** Valuation and prospective earnings Visual inspection: not performed.
- **Gold double bottom:** Conditional technical pattern Visual inspection: not performed.

## Framework lessons

- A monetary denominator is not a consumption-price denominator.
- A useful framework distinguishes national monetary sovereignty from conditional union-wide support.

## Verification limitations

- Current page snapshot is not an authenticated publication-date version.
- A missing horizon is not replaced with an invented author deadline.
- Market sensitivities use vendor adjusted closes and do not reconstruct portfolio execution.
